headline: Single-cell multiomics resolve cell-type regulation across tissues, species and age
label: Single Cell Omics Methods
summary: Atlas-scale single-cell references now span the human lifespan and non-model species, enabling cell-type regulatory comparisons across tissues and donors.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell and multiomic profiling used to resolve cell-type-specific regulation across tissues, donors and age. An integrated human lung atlas combines over 18 million cells from 253 datasets across the lifespan, defining 142 cell types. A multi-omics scRNA and snATAC atlas of human RPE and choroid from 102 donors aged 0 to 99 years links AMD GWAS variants to LIPG and COL4A3. A single-nucleus atlas of adult laying hen liver extends this approach to a non-model species and reports that enhanced genome annotation improves transcript detection and hepatocyte subpopulation resolution. Single-cell tools also deconvolve 9p21 transcripts (p16INK4A, p14ARF, p15INK4B) and map cis-regulatory elements, showing independent expression across tissues. The PFAS hepatotoxicity study integrates public RNA-seq with target prediction and network inference and does not share this single-cell framing. What is new is atlas-scale coverage across lifespan and species, together with annotation-driven gains in transcript resolution.
